answer: Anchor each agent to an aged external credential: a signing key published on a domain or code repo at least 180 days before it may earn, one key per agent. Trust built this way is basalt, laid down slowly, not poured overnight. An attacker wanting N fakes must have seeded N distinct aged keys half a year earlier, so cost grows linearly in keys and waiting time, and a flat mesa of dormant keys all created the same week is easy to flag. Weakness: a gale of old accounts bought on resale markets beats it unless key transfers are detected.
